469e69c2-0031-5e2a-98be-7540eec6b434.name: Autoworld Brussels
469e69c2-0031-5e2a-98be-7540eec6b434.description:
**Presentation of Autoworld**  
  
Autoworld, a renowned automobile museum nestled in Brussels, Belgium, is a must-visit for car enthusiasts, history buffs and tourists alike. Situated within the historic Cinquantenaire Park, the museum offers a comprehensive journey through the evolution of the automobile.  
  
**A Rich History and Mission**  
  
Founded in 1986, Autoworld is dedicated to preserving and showcasing the rich heritage of the automotive industry. The museum houses a vast collection of over 250 vehicles, spanning from late 19th-century models to modern-day supercars.  
  
**Collections and Exhibitions**  
  
Autoworld's collection features iconic brands such as Bugatti, Bentley, Ferrari, Rolls-Royce and Mercedes-Benz. However, the museum doesn't just focus on top brands. It also highlights various types of cars, offering visitors a diverse perspective on automotive history. Each exhibition is carefully curated with innovative and engaging displays.  
  
Beyond its permanent collection, Autoworld regularly hosts temporary exhibitions that delve into specific themes, brands or eras. These exhibitions often feature multimedia presentations, rare artifacts and interactive displays.  
  
**A Cultural and Educational Hub**  
  
Autoworld plays a crucial role in preserving the cultural significance of the automobile. It serves as an educational institution, offering guided tours, workshops and events for visitors of all ages. The museum strives to create an immersive and memorable experience for every visitor.  
  
**Entertainment and Community Engagement**  
  
Autoworld is more than just a museum. It actively participates in community events and seeks to provide entertaining and engaging experiences for everyone. Families are particularly welcomed, with activities and exhibitions designed to delight visitors of all ages.  
  
**Conclusion**  
  
Autoworld is a living celebration of automotive heritage. Whether you're a car aficionado or simply curious about the evolution of transportation, Autoworld promises an enriching experience that is both educational and entertaining.

54d1c525-6d97-5d76-b845-4944959e1802.name: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum (FBQ Museums)
54d1c525-6d97-5d76-b845-4944959e1802.description:
Founded in 1998 by H.E. Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani, the Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum (FBQ) is the Sheikh’s brainchild and a monument to his enduring passion for collecting international items of peculiar and historical relevance.  
  
A museum with a global perspective, FBQ brings together over 30,000 objects from across the ages and a multitude of cultures. It represents, in effect, a modern version of a ‘Cabinet of Curiosities’, the historic and eclectic room of marvels from the Renaissance.  
  
The journey through more than 30 galleries ranges from the prehistoric to the present day, encompassing several themes: Islamic art, Qatari heritage, carpets, weapons, vehicles, jewellery and currency. Gallery highlights also include a rebuilt Syrian house and the Quran room. The artefacts showcased in FBQ’s galleries embody Islam’s visual culture and its far-reaching traditions from southern Europe, North Africa, the Middle East and South Asia. The thematic presentation of the works draws attention to the similarities of artistic forms and cultural expressions and their interdependence among societies.  
  
FBQ is much more than a museum. Since the construction of the main museum in Al Shahaniya in 1998 using local stone and traditional turrets, FBQ has been fulfilling the museum founder’s aim to create and share a new cultural heritage for Qatar and beyond. With the establishment of the Carpet Museum in the heart of Doha in 2014 and the addition of the Car Museum, the FBQ complex of museums aims to inspire people to engage with cultural heritage by sharing stories from near and far. FBQ strives to foster cross-cultural dialogue through exhibitions, education and public programs, both locally and internationally.  
  
In 2010, the museum was selected by Qatar’s Ministry of Arts, Culture, and Heritage as one of the cultural landmarks of the ‘Doha 2010 Capital of Culture’ activities.

60a55c2b-0e32-50e4-b8c5-751993ac2e4f.name: Museo Nazionale dell’Automobile
60a55c2b-0e32-50e4-b8c5-751993ac2e4f.description:
Founded in 1933 by Carlo Biscaretti di Ruffia, the Museo Nazionale dell’Automobile (MAUTO) preserves a collection of over 200 original cars from eighty different brands, showcasing the evolution of an invention that changed the world. The collection spans from steam carriages of the late 19th century to the design masterpieces of the 1950s, including iconic racing champions and prototypes that have shaped the future of automotive research. Thanks to an impressive setting, each car is brought back to its original splendour, guiding visitors on a journey through historical moments, cultural movements, technological advancements and scientific discoveries—all influenced by the automobile's constant drive for innovation.  
  
Opened to the public in 1960 in a building designed by architect Amedeo Albertini, the Museum underwent a major renovation in 2007 in preparation for the 150th anniversary of Italian unification. Once renovations were finished in 2011, MAUTO reopened with a new layout that earned it a place among *The Times'* list of *World's 50 Best Museums*. Today, the Museum is an internationally recognized hub for automotive culture.  
  
Supported by institutions and research organizations, the Museum produces two major exhibitions a year. It also hosts installations by experimental artists and temporary projects in the Project Room, and organizes talks, projections, concerts, guided tours and workshops for schools and families.  
  
The Museum is also home to a Documentation Centre for archival and research activities and a Conservation and Restoration Centre, dedicated to preserving and restoring historic vehicles.

71ca5109-9020-572c-ba08-de39cf6a95a0.name: Ankara Toy Museum
71ca5109-9020-572c-ba08-de39cf6a95a0.description:
Ankara Toy Museum, located in Ankara University, was founded on 20 April 1990 by  
Bekir Onur. The museum has an impressive collection of almost 3000 toys, which  
are displayed in five distinct sections; traditional toys; mass produced toys; imported toys; antique toys; and the latest toys. Whilst the museum contains a wide range of children's playthings, the most important feature of the collection is its notable selection of traditional toys. This museum is dedicated to carry out three fundamental functions:  
a) To protect those toys under threat of disappearing in a rapidly changing world  
b) To make further study of the history of play, childhood, education, culture, and  
industrial history through the medium of play.  
c) To aid in the design of innovative educational programmes, aimed specifically at  
children, in the fields of museum, art, history, and science.  
  
For most of its history, from 1990 to 2015, the museum was hosted in a building  
belonging to the Faculty of Educational Sciences. However, In 2015 the museum was relocated to its current structure, allowing curators to use the period between July and October of that year to extensively revise exhibition designs and concepts. Originally, the museum had displayed its toy collection based on material types, but has since moved to a system focused more on individual toy types.  
  
The mission of the museum is to provide sustainable sources to study and protect the history of toy and play, with a particular focus on the cultural heritage of children in Turkey. Furthermore, the museum continually strives to improve, maintain and exhibit its toy collection within the museum.  
  
The museum defined its vision as: To be a child friendly museum whose aim is to produce for children with children; to focus on the history of toys and culture of children; and finally to provide programs and events for learning through practical activities.

84930941-c58c-5d5a-8c1d-5caa589aecd2.name: Birzeit University Museum
84930941-c58c-5d5a-8c1d-5caa589aecd2.description:
Birzeit University Museum is an innovative art space at the heart of the Birzeit University campus. It seeks to produce contemporary art and promote its practice in the university community and Palestinian society, through a multidisciplinary, experimental approach. The museum’s mission rests on the belief that art practice is an active means of generating progressive ideas and supporting social advancement.  
  
Established in 1997, the museum’s initial aim was to preserve two main collections, the unique Tawfiq Canaan Collection of Amulets and Talismans and the Palestinian Costumes, acquired by the university in the 1980s.  
  
The first artwork collection was assembled from works donated by Swiss artist Rene Feurer, Syrian artist Marwan Qassab Bashi and many others. Since the opening of its first gallery in 2005, the museum has become an open artistic space, offering several artistic exhibitions as well as an e-library.  
  
The museum now houses over 2,100 pieces that include an art collection as well as the original amulet and costume collections. These collections are used as a material and visual source of knowledge, exploring the notions of history, identity, heritage and much more.  
  
In addition to its many physical galleries, the museum includes the Virtual Gallery, which was established as an online archive for Palestinian art practice. Launched in 2005, and available in both Arabic and English, its objective is to offer a window on contemporary art in Palestine. The online gallery includes a library, previews of exhibitions, artist portfolios, talks ‎and seminars. It also includes a database of rare art and ethnographic collections.

89f613d2-8723-5be8-8e46-487f9dae46f4.name: Swiss National Museum
89f613d2-8723-5be8-8e46-487f9dae46f4.description: Three museums – the National Museum Zurich, the Château de Prangins and the Forum of Swiss History Schwyz – as well as the collections centre in Affoltern am Albis – are united under the umbrella of the Swiss National Museum (SNM). The permanent exhibitions at the museums present Swiss history from its beginnings to the present, and give an insight into Swiss identities and the rich tapestry of our country’s history and culture. Temporary exhibitions on current topics add to the experience.

8fd06198-6d39-5611-a37e-45ac296ac304.name: Museum of Russian Icons
8fd06198-6d39-5611-a37e-45ac296ac304.description:
In the 1960’s, plastics engineer Gordon B. Lankton went to work at Nypro, an international injection molded plastics company, in Clinton, Massachusetts. In 1989, on a business trip to Russia, Mr. Lankton purchased his first icon at an open-air market. His collection quickly grew, and eventually gave birth to the idea of starting a museum. Mr. Lankton chose Clinton for the location to give back to the community that had supported him.  
  
The Museum is housed in a 150-year-old former mill building. Three floors of galleries display the permanent collection. A dedicated gallery features special exhibitions ranging from contemporary Russian art to icons from other Orthodox cultures. It is the only museum in the USA dedicated to Russian icons, and the largest collection of icons outside of Russia.  
  
An icon is an image of a holy person or event, created by an iconographer who follows the strict standards of the Orthodox Church. Most of the objects in the Museum’s collection are created with paint on wooden board; icons can also be made in other materials, including mosaic, fresco, embroidery, and metal. Iconography is a living tradition, and icons today are painted in the same way that they have been for hundreds of years. The Museum collection includes icons dating to the 1400s to contemporary icons painted in the last few years, with the majority dating from the 17th to 19th centuries.  
  
MISSION  
The Museum of Russian Icons inspires the appreciation and study of Russian culture by collecting and exhibiting icons and related objects; igniting the interest of national and international audiences; and offering interactive educational programs. The Museum serves as a leading center for research and scholarship through the Center for Icon Studies and other institutional collaborations.

b3e9f4b0-6de0-5987-880c-3509dd312e9c.name: Museu do Caramulo
b3e9f4b0-6de0-5987-880c-3509dd312e9c.description:
The town of Caramulo was born in 1921 on the southern side of the eponymous mountain range after a doctor, Jerónimo de Lacerda, founded a sanatorium resort; it was the largest in the Iberian Peninsula. Even in its early years, Caramulo was a magnificent location, unique in its advanced infrastructure compared to the rest of Portugal: by 1938 it had running water, an exemplary network of urban sewers (and the respective treatment station) and a waste collection system with a crematorium. A hydroelectric power station provided electricity. Caramulo also had an unusual urban plan, with wide roads with sidewalks, green spaces and public gardens of incomparable beauty and in a proportion never seen before.  
  
It was here that, in 1921 and 1923, two children of Dr. Jerónimo de Lacerda, Abel and João, were born. Aware that medical progress would make the Caramulo treatment centre obsolete, Abel, who had become an economist, and his brother João, a doctor, started looking for ideas that would ensure the survival of their father’s work. They decided to transform the existing sanatorium into a centre for high-altitude tourism, converting the mountain scenery into a hub for culture and art. After all, the location was excellent: a mountain in the centre of Portugal, with lush vegetation, facing south over an extensive valley – the widest panorama in the country.  
  
It was with this idea in mind that Abel and João de Lacerda founded, in the 1950s, an unusual museum. Abel de Lacerda, passionate about art, constructed a building incorporating the most modern concepts of museology to exhibit an unusual 500-piece collection consisting of paintings, sculptures, furniture, ceramics and tapestries, ranging from ancient Egypt to Picasso. João de Lacerda, passionate about automobiles, constructed an adjoining building designed to exhibit 100 automobiles and motorcycles, under the principle that all vehicles could be easily left for exhibition and conservation.  
  
With the premature death of Abel in 1957, the Abel de Lacerda Foundation was created – though now it’s known as the Abel Foundation and João de Lacerda. The Foundation is the current owner of the Museu do Caramulo. Open to the public all year, the Museu do Caramulo has received over one and a half million visitors since its inauguration.  
  
The building planned by Abel Lacerda to house precious donated antiques was inaugurated by the President of the Republic in 1959. It was one of the first museums designed and made entirely in Portugal, and its structure represented the latest design principles in museology.
